status.holdout: v2 failed its holdout (July 2024 - June 2026, run once): 0.81 of actual defaults under the recorded check, 0.92 counted correctly (L-038, L-039).
status.overlay: No overlay (Option B): the LGD model's conservatism (1.64x the real loss per default, L-033) more than offsets the default shortfall (0.74 in loss terms). The +34% default uplift is shown as a sensitivity.
status.framing: Educational model on Freddie Mac conforming mortgages (sample book). Not an audited bank reserve and not accounting advice.

models.name: Default and payoff (PD and prepayment)
models.how: Monthly logistic transition models from the loan's delinquency state (current, 30, 60 days late), played forward by path simulation, 8 paths per loan

models.name: Loss given default (LGD)
models.how: Two steps: the chance of any loss, then its size; monotone trees tied to the loan-to-value and house prices

models.name: Exposure at default (EAD)
models.how: The payment schedule plus partial prepayment by loan age

models.name: CECL engine
models.how: PD x LGD x EAD for every loan and month to maturity; Fed scenarios published by the reserve date; 24-month forecast, 12-month reversion; weights 60/30/10
models.status: Built; tie-outs and rollforwards to the cent

models.name: Adverse path
models.how: Halfway between the Fed's baseline and severely adverse paths

limits.text: v2 failed its holdout: defaults short in 2024-2026, worst in the newest vintages.
The LGD predicts 1.64 times the real loss per default (resolved 2017-2021 defaults).
The check used in the exams under-counted projected defaults; counted correctly, v2 over-projects in calm years.
The crisis exam failed: like any data-driven model, v2 under-reacts to a kind of downturn it has not seen.
After year 3 the loss runs at the month-36 chances and the long-run economy.
Conforming Freddie Mac loans only: no subprime, jumbo, commercial or card loans.
Mortgage-rate shocks lower the reserve slightly in both directions.

definitionOfDefault: 90+ days late, a real-estate-owned acquisition, or a loss-event payoff; payment pauses for disasters and COVID stop the delinquency clock.
